sentences.text: Heard on I.A. No.887 of 2024, which is an application for taking additional documents taken on record.

2. Documents may be relevant for proper adjudication of this appeal, therefore, I.A. is allowed and documents are taken on record.
3. Also heard on I.A. No.1929 of 2024, which is fifth repeat application under Section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the sole appellant - Deepak.
4.
The fourth application for suspension of sentence filed on behalf of the appellant was dismissed on merit by this Court.

5. This appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved by the judgment d a t e d 28.08.2019 passed by learned I Additional Sessions Judge Biaora, District Rajgarh in Special S.T. No.387/2018,
whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offence under Sections 363 and 376(D)(a) of IPC and Section 5(G) read with Section 6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo 7 years R.I., life imprisonment and 10 years R.I. with fine of Rs.2,000/-, Rs.3,000/- and 2000/- respectively with default stipulation.
6.

sentences.text: As per the prosecution story, co-accused Ram Bharose along with present appellant Deepak Shivhare abducted the prosecutrix on motorcycle, thereafter, they took her to Dhaba and gave her some sedative.
When she became unconscious, then they committed rape upon her.
After gaining the conscious, the Dhaba owner has informed her about the commission of rape by the two accused persons.
She went to the Police Station along with her uncle and lodged an FIR.

sentences.text: As per the DNA Report, male profile were also found.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant has preferred that cross examination of PW-1 in Para 25 and 26,
she has specifically admitted that appellant Deepak has not committed any sexual assault.
The main allegation is against the Ram Bharose, which has been established by DNA report also.
Appellant has been convicted under Section 363 of IPC in which the maximum punishment is 7 years, out of which he has undergone more than five and half years in the jail.
The appeal is of the year 2019 and there is no likelihood of its final hearing in near future.
He, therefore, prays for suspension of jail sentence and release him on bail.
8 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application for suspension of sentence and prays for its rejection.
9. Counsel for the complainant submits that complainant has no objection if sentence is suspended and bail is granted to appellant.

10. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
11.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties, nature and gravity of the allegation against the appellant and that final conclusion of this appeal will take a long sufficient time, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant.

12. Accordingly, IA No.1929 of 2024 is allowed and the execution of remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended till the final disposal of this appeal and it is ordered that the appellant be released on bail on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and upon furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 04.11.2024 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard during the pendency of this Appeal.
13. Registry is directed to list the matte for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
(VIVEK RUSIA)
